results.title: CT and VT (PT) Wiring Checks / Never open-circuit an energized CT secondary
results.text: A current transformer drives current into its burden. If the secondary is opened while primary current flows, the secondary voltage can rise to thousands of volts, which is a shock hazard and can destroy the CT. Use the shorting terminal block to short the CT secondary before disconnecting a relay or meter, and confirm the shorting screws or links are installed correctly.

results.title: CT and VT (PT) Wiring Checks / CT ratio and secondary current
results.text: CT ratio is primary amps to secondary amps, for example 600:5. Primary current = secondary current × (ratio primary / ratio secondary). With a 600:5 CT, 4 A secondary equals 480 A primary. If a relay or meter reads a value that is off by a constant factor, check that the CT ratio setting in the device matches the CT tap actually wired on a multi-ratio CT.

results.title: Protective Relay Testing (Acceptance and Maintenance Concepts) / Secondary injection testing
results.text: Relays are tested by injecting secondary current and voltage from a test set into the relay inputs, with the relay isolated from the CTs, VTs and trip circuits using test switches. Short the CT circuits and open the trip outputs before injecting, so the test does not trip in-service breakers or open-circuit a CT.
